## ExperimentalTestimonials + LogoCarousel — marquees moved to the compositor (mobile)
- CAUSE: both were framer `animate={{x:["-50%","0%"]}}` with `repeat: Infinity` — framer
  writes `transform` from JS every frame on its own rAF, so any main-thread stall stutters
  them. Same root cause as the LogoLoop marquee fixed earlier.
- FIX: the travel is a clean **-50%** (each track holds exactly two copies, so -50% is
  precisely one copy), which means a CSS keyframe needs NO measurement — unlike the
  LogoLoop fix, which had to thread a measured pixel width through `--logoloop-seq`.
  Added `@keyframes marquee-half` + `.marquee-half` to globals.css, scoped in CSS to
  `@media (width < 48rem)`, plus a `prefers-reduced-motion` override.
- DESKTOP SAFETY BY CONSTRUCTION: the rule lives inside a media query, so it can never run
  on desktop even during the `useIsDesktop()` false-on-first-render flip. framer is gated
  `isDesktop ? … : undefined` on both components; desktop keeps its exact previous
  behaviour (arrow pagination / 28s framer loop).
- **BLAST RADIUS**: `LogoCarousel` is shared by 12 pages (per the map), so this mobile-only
  perf fix lands on all of them. Same visuals everywhere; flagged to the user.
- **DEV SERVER WAS SERVING STALE CSS — 3 grounded-loops attempts, then changed approach.**
  Symptom: `animationName: none` with the rule absent from every stylesheet
  (`ruleCount: 0`) while `matchMedia('(width < 48rem)')` matched. Discriminated with curl:
  the served `src_app_globals_0p2ml0n.css` had **4** hits for the `no-scrollbar` rule added
  earlier this session but **0** for `marquee-half` — so globals.css HAD compiled before
  and has stopped recompiling. Likely my own concurrent `bunx next build` runs (the map
  warns about exactly this). The :3000 dev server is external to this session, so I did not
  kill a process I did not start — verified against a production build instead.
- VERIFIED via `next build` output CSS: `@keyframes marquee-half{0%{transform:translate(-50%)}
  to{transform:translate(0)}}` and `@media not all and (min-width:48rem){.marquee-half{...}}`
  — the compiled form of `width < 48rem`, i.e. mobile only.
- VERIFIED at runtime on `next start -p 3001` (server stopped afterwards), 390px: BOTH
  tracks `animation-name: marquee-half`, `linear`, `infinite`, `will-change: transform`,
  1 CSS animation object each with `playState: "running"` and keyframes
  `translate(-50%) -> translate(0px)`; durations **40s** (testimonials) and **28s**
  (logoCarousel) from `--marquee-duration`; framer inline transform EMPTY on both.
  Child counts 8 and 22 — both even, so -50% is exactly one copy and the loop is seamless.
- VERIFIED 1265px: `animation-name: none` on both (CSS off), and framer writes an inline
  `transform` there while writing nothing on mobile — that empty-vs-present difference is
  the direct proof of which engine owns each breakpoint.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` 0; biome clean on both changed components; `next build` ✓.
- ACTION FOR USER: restart the :3000 dev server — it will keep serving the old CSS
  (no marquee) until it does.

## Marquees — moved from a globals.css keyframe to WAAPI in the component (my bug)
- MY BUG, user-reported: after the previous entry the mobile carousels were STATIC. Cause
  was not the code — it was that I put the animation in `globals.css`, and this dev server
  had stopped recompiling that file. Proven with curl against the URL the page actually
  references: served `src_app_globals_0p2ml0n.css` had **0** hits for `marquee-half` and
  **4** for `no-scrollbar` (added earlier the same session), i.e. it compiled once and then
  went stale. Telling the user to restart was not a fix; the fragility was mine.
- FIX: `useMarqueeHalf(ref, seconds, enabled)` exported from `ui/LogoCarousel.tsx`, used by
  both LogoCarousel and ExperimentalTestimonials. It runs the identical -50% -> 0 travel via
  `element.animate()` (Web Animations API). WAAPI transform animations are composited
  exactly like CSS keyframes — same perf — but they ship with the COMPONENT, so a stale
  stylesheet can never freeze them again. Honours `prefers-reduced-motion` with a live
  listener; cancels on unmount and whenever `enabled` goes false.
- `@keyframes marquee-half` + `.marquee-half` deleted from globals.css and both class
  usages removed, so there is exactly one mechanism (grep for `marquee-half` outside the
  hook name returns nothing).
- **LESSON (generalise this):** prefer component-carried animation over a globals.css rule
  in this repo. globals.css has gone stale mid-session more than once; TSX always rebuilds.
  The LogoLoop marquee still depends on a globals.css keyframe (`logoloop-marquee`) — it
  works only because it compiled BEFORE the stylesheet froze. Worth migrating if it ever
  goes static.
- VERIFIED on the DEV SERVER the user is actually looking at (not just a prod build),
  390px: both tracks carry exactly 1 animation, `playState: "running"`, `easing: linear`,
  `iterations === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` (asserted — `getTiming()` serialises Infinity
  as null in JSON, which is a reporting artifact, not a bug), keyframes
  `translate3d(-50%,0,0) -> translate3d(0,0,0)`, durations **40000ms** (testimonials, 8
  children) and **28000ms** (logoCarousel, 22 children); both child counts even, so -50%
  is exactly one copy. framer's inline transform EMPTY on both.
- VERIFIED 1265px: **0** WAAPI animations on both tracks (hook disabled by `!isDesktop`)
  and framer writes the inline transform instead — desktop still on its original path.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` 0; biome clean on both files; `next build` ✓.

## ExperimentalTestimonials — marquee made draggable (mobile), still auto-moving
- APPROACH: drag SCRUBS THE ANIMATION'S OWN TIMELINE rather than maintaining a separate
  offset. The track is two identical copies and the WAAPI animation runs -50% -> 0 over one
  period, so one period == exactly one copy and `currentTime` can be wrapped modulo the
  period with no visible seam. pointerdown pauses + records `currentTime`; pointermove maps
  px -> ms linearly (`delta = dx / halfWidth * period`); pointerup resumes. No inline
  transform juggling, no rAF, no state — a pointermove writes one number and the compositor
  keeps painting.
- Chose this over converting to a native `overflow-x-auto` scroller (the PortfolioSection
  pattern) because that would have turned a CONTINUOUS marquee into a stepped carousel;
  here the auto-motion is the point. Trade-off: no release-inertia, unlike native scroll —
  releasing simply resumes the marquee.
- `touch-action: pan-y` is set on the track while draggable (and restored on cleanup) so
  the page still scrolls vertically while horizontal drags reach the handler.
- Drag is OPT-IN via a 4th arg — `useMarqueeHalf(ref, seconds, enabled, draggable)`.
  LogoCarousel keeps `draggable` false, so the 12 pages using it are unaffected.
- VERIFIED 390px with a synthetic drag: playState `running` -> **`paused` on pointerdown**
  -> **`running` on pointerup**; a 100px leftward drag moved currentTime by **-3165ms**
  against an expected `(-100/1264)*40000 = -3165ms` (asserted equal within 1ms);
  `touch-action: pan-y`.
- WRAP EDGE VERIFIED: from t=500ms a leftward drag landed at **37335ms**, i.e. wrapped up
  near the 40000ms period instead of going negative.
- ISOLATION VERIFIED: the same synthetic drag on the LogoCarousel track left its
  `currentTime` unchanged, playState `running`, `touch-action: auto` — drag really is
  opt-in.
- VERIFIED 1265px: **0** WAAPI animations, `touch-action: auto`, and a synthetic drag left
  the transform untouched — desktop still on framer's arrow pagination.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` 0; biome clean on both files; `next build` ✓.

## ExperimentalTestimonials drag — rewritten, my previous version was the lag
- TWO REAL DEFECTS IN MY OWN DRAG CODE, both on the per-move hot path:
  1. `onMove` called `el.getBoundingClientRect()` on EVERY pointermove — a forced layout
     read, then immediately mutated `currentTime` (a style write). Read-after-write thrash
     on every single event, at whatever rate the touchscreen fires.
  2. Scrubbing `currentTime` on a PAUSED WAAPI animation is not composited — pausing drops
     the animation off the compositor, so each scrub repainted the full 2528px track (8
     cards with borders, gradients, shadows).
- REWRITE: drag now cancels the animation and writes `transform` directly.
  * `half` measured ONCE at pointerdown; zero layout reads during the drag.
  * pointermove only updates a number and schedules one rAF; N moves in a frame collapse
    to ONE style write (`paint`).
  * `will-change: transform` held for the drag so the element keeps its compositor layer;
    cleared on release.
  * position <-> time is linear (`x = half * (t/period - 1)`), so release recreates the
    animation at the matching time — no jump. x is wrapped into [-half, 0) and the two
    copies are identical, so wrapping is invisible.
- VERIFIED 390px, instrumenting `getBoundingClientRect` to count forced layouts:
  **1 layout read at pointerdown, 0 added by 20 pointermoves**; `animations during drag: 0`
  (cancelled, so nothing fights the inline transform); `will-change: transform` set;
  inline transform `translate3d(-948px, 0, 0)` at pointerdown; the 20 moves left the
  transform untouched, proving they were deferred to the coalescing rAF.
  On release: 1 animation, `running`, resume time **6994ms vs 6994ms expected** for the
  net -95px drag; inline transform AND will-change both cleared.
- VERIFIED 1265px: 0 WAAPI animations, `touch-action: auto`, `will-change` unset, and a
  synthetic drag left the transform unchanged — desktop still on framer pagination.
  LogoCarousel also untouched (0 animations, `touch-action: auto`).
- PANE NOTE: my first probe timed out because it awaited `requestAnimationFrame`, which
  never fires here (0 frames in 14s, measured earlier). Consequence: the drag's visual
  update cannot be observed in-pane at all — `paint` only runs on a real rAF. Everything
  above is the wiring, measured; the smoothness itself needs the phone.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` 0; biome clean; `next build` ✓.

## PortfolioSection autoplay — three fixes; motion NOT verifiable in-pane
- USER: "it is not self moving". Drag was fine (native scroll), autoplay was not running.
- LIKELIEST CAUSE, and the substantive fix: the pause guard was bound to `touchstart`
  and paused for a FIXED 6s after ANY touch — including the incidental touches of
  scrolling the PAGE past the carousel. With a 4.5s tick that is up to ~10s of stillness
  after every swipe, which on a phone reads as "never moves". Now it pauses only while the
  pointer is actually DOWN (`pointerdown`/`wheel` hold; `pointerup`/`pointercancel`/`wheel`
  release) and resumes **1.5s** after the finger lifts (was 6s).
- ALSO CHANGED:
  * Autoplay drives `scrollLeft` with a 600ms rAF tween (easeInOutCubic) instead of
    `scrollTo({behavior:"smooth"})`. Smooth scroll was the one link with no guarantee —
    ignored in some mobile browsers, and it fights `scroll-snap-type: mandatory`. Snap is
    set to `none` for the tween's duration and restored at the end so it lands the slide.
  * Stale-tween self-heal: if a tween's rAF never runs (backgrounded/throttled renderer),
    `tween` stayed non-zero and blocked autoplay FOREVER. `advance` now reclaims a tween
    that has overshot 3x its duration. I watched this exact deadlock happen in the pane.
- **HONEST VERIFICATION LIMIT — autoplay motion could NOT be exercised here at all.**
  Three independent pane failures conspire, each measured with a control in the same run:
  1. rAF frozen — `rafFramesInRun: 0` over 15s (it fired once in a moment when the pane
     was briefly visible, then went back to 0).
  2. IntersectionObserver latched — it delivers no callbacks, so `visible` stays at its
     mount-time value (false, section below the fold). Even after `scrollIntoView` put the
     track in the viewport (`trackInViewport: true`), tween starts stayed **0**.
  3. `scrollTo({behavior:"smooth"})` frozen (measured in an earlier task).
  A `pauseHoldsWhileFingerDown: true` reading was DISCARDED as evidence, not reported as a
  pass: zero tweens would have started regardless, so it proves nothing.
- WHAT IS VERIFIED: `bunx tsc --noEmit` 0; biome 2 errors == 2 on the HEAD copy (parity);
  `next build` ✓; declaration order of `stopTween` before `advance` asserted by index.
- VERIFIED 1265px: `overflow-x: visible`, `scroll-snap-type: none`, inline snap never
  touched, GSAP transform intact, track 6400px, and a synthetic pointerdown/up left
  scrollLeft unchanged — the mobile effect is not wired on desktop at all.
- The three fixes are reasoned, not observed. If it still does not move on the phone, the
  next thing to check is whether autoplay is being gated by `visible` (IntersectionObserver)
  rather than by the pause guard.

## PortfolioSection autoplay — FOUND IT: the async gates were latching
- ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by measurement, not reasoning this time): autoplay was gated on
  two flags set by ASYNC CALLBACKS — `visible` from an IntersectionObserver, and `paused`
  cleared by a setTimeout. If a callback never arrived, the flag latched and autoplay was
  dead permanently with no path back. In the pane the IO never delivers, so `visible`
  stayed false forever and `advance` reached `animateTo` **0 times**. Same class of failure
  on a phone: a `pointerdown` whose `pointerup`/`pointercancel` is swallowed (the browser
  taking over a scroll gesture) latched `paused` the same way.
- FIX — every gate is now a SYNCHRONOUS check made at tick time, so nothing can go stale:
  * visibility: `getBoundingClientRect()` in `advance` (one layout read per 4.5s tick)
    instead of an IntersectionObserver flag.
  * interaction: a `lastInteraction` TIMESTAMP instead of a boolean cleared by a timer;
    `pointerDown` additionally expires after 5s so a missing pointerup cannot stall it.
  * IntersectionObserver and the resume `setTimeout` are gone entirely.
- **MOTION VERIFIED END-TO-END for the first time** (390px). The pane's rAF is frozen, so
  a working rAF was supplied; the stale-tween guard reclaimed the tween that had stalled on
  the frozen one and the next tick ran on the shim. scrollLeft trail:
  **0 -> 4 -> 21 -> 88 -> 220 -> 316 -> 371 -> 388 -> 390** — an easeInOutCubic curve
  landing exactly on the 390px slide boundary; 23 rAF schedules for one 600ms tween;
  `slidesAdvanced: 1`, `landedOnSlideBoundary: true`. That also proves the stale-tween
  guard works, since without it the first stalled tween would have blocked everything.
- BEFORE/AFTER on the same measurement: `animateTo` reached **0 times** with the IO gate,
  **>=1 and then actually completing** with the rect gate.
- VERIFIED 1265px over a 10s window spanning two autoplay intervals: `overflow-x: visible`,
  `scroll-snap-type: none`, inline snap never touched, scrollLeft unchanged, GSAP transform
  intact, track 6400px — the mobile effect never fires on desktop.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` 0; biome 2 errors == HEAD parity; `next build` ✓.
- LESSON: prefer a synchronous check at use-time over a flag maintained by an async
  callback for anything that gates a loop. A missed callback is unrecoverable; a stale read
  is self-correcting.

## Footer wordmark — fix BOTH clips on mobile (my regression from the previous task)
- MY REGRESSION: unhiding the wordmark last task exposed a desktop-tuned element to mobile,
  and my `max-md:py-0` removed the room its descenders needed.
- CLIP 1, VERTICAL (what the user screenshotted — the `g`): each letter span is
  `overflow-hidden` with `pb-[0.3em] -mb-[0.3em]`, so the descender renders BELOW the h1's
  own box; the wrapper is also `overflow-hidden`, so with `py-0` it cut exactly there.
  MEASURED: letter box sat **21.0px** past the wrapper's clip edge, against
  `0.3em x 70.2px = 21.1px` of descender room — the numbers identify the cause outright.
  FIX: `max-md:py-0` -> `max-md:pt-0 max-md:pb-6` (24px > 21.1px). Top stays 0 because the
  parent supplies `max-md:gap-12`.
- CLIP 2, HORIZONTAL (found by measurement, NOT visible to me in the screenshot): the
  wordmark was **338px wide inside a 318px overflow-hidden box**, shaving the S and the
  final e. `text-[18vw]` is sized for the desktop container; below md the wrapper loses a
  FIXED ~72px to page padding, so the vw multiplier has to drop.
  FIX: `max-md:text-[15vw]`.
- WHY 15 AND NOT 16: because the lost padding is fixed, the narrowest phone sets the limit.
  16vw measured **-0.7px slack at 320px** — still clipping, and it only passed an earlier
  assertion because that check used a +-1px tolerance. Tightened to 15vw and re-measured.
- VERIFIED 390px: font 58.5px, width 283 in a 318 box, **35.1px** horizontal slack, 6.5px
  vertical slack, `clippedLetters: []`, all 10 letters rendered.
- VERIFIED 320px: font 48px, width 234 in a 248 box, **14.4px** horizontal slack, 9.6px
  vertical, `clippedLetters: []`.
- VERIFIED 1265px: padding 40/80px, `order: 0`, font **230.4px**. NOTE: that equals 18vw of
  **1280**, not of `clientWidth` 1265 — `vw` units include the scrollbar. An assertion
  comparing against clientWidth reported a false mismatch; the code is correct.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` 0; biome 2 errors == 2 on HEAD; `next build` ✓.

## ExperimentalTestimonials — rotating word animates on mobile too
- Same shape as the AboutSection/RotatingWord case: an `isDesktop ? <AnimatePresence…> :
  <static rotatingWords[0]>` branch meant mobile rendered a frozen first word, while the

  `isDesktop` is still used 6x elsewhere in the file (marquee gate, arrows), so nothing
  dangles.

  reported as laggy in AboutSection: the gradient + `bg-clip-text` moved OFF the animated
  element onto a STATIC child, and `will-change: transform, opacity` set statically. A
  background-clipped element cannot be cheaply composited, so animating it re-rasterises
  the glyph-clipped gradient every frame; as a child it rasterises once and the parent
  layer is merely translated.
- DESKTOP PROVEN UNCHANGED BY BEFORE/AFTER, not by argument: captured a baseline at 1265px
  BEFORE editing, re-measured after, and diffed — **8/8 metrics equal, `mismatches: []`**

  background-clip text, colour rgba(0,0,0,0)). Structure confirmed moved:
  `animatedHasBgClip: false`, `gradientChildHasBgClip: true`.
- VERIFIED 390px: the animated element now carries framer's inline
  `will-change:transform, opacity; opacity:0; transform:translateX(-100%)` — the static
  branch had NO style attribute at all, so this is direct proof the animated branch is
  live. Appearance intact: gradient on the static child, transparent colour, 36px, mask
  and overflow-hidden still on the wrapper.
- Word cycling itself is not observable in-pane (frozen animation clock; `mode="wait"`

## Homepage - remove entry animations below md

- Added `useIsMobile()` + `NO_ENTRY` to `src/lib/useIsDesktop.ts`. Unlike
  `useIsDesktop` (which starts false everywhere and only flips in an effect),
  `useIsMobile` reads matchMedia in a lazy `useState` initializer, so it is
  already correct on the first client render - before framer consumes `initial`.
- Gated only the `transition` prop: `transition={isMobile ? NO_ENTRY : {...}}`.
  This is deliberate. The repo's existing `initial={isDesktop ? {...} : false}`
  pattern kills the animation on DESKTOP too, because `initial` is read at mount
  when `isDesktop` is still false - measured at 1265px, every already-gated
  element (#about, testimonials outer) renders with `style: null` and never
  animates. Applying that pattern to the ungated components would have changed
  desktop, which the task forbids. `transition` also emits no SSR markup, so the
  mount-correct hook cannot trip hydration.
- Files: Herosection (6 mount entries), ServiceSection (3), Testimonials (5),
  ContactSection (5), BlogSection (3), Footer (4 + the wordmark). Footer's
  wordmark uses variants, so it got `brandContainerInstant`/`brandLetterInstant`
  twins whose `hidden` states are byte-identical to the originals - only the
  `visible` transition differs, which emits nothing at SSR.
- Untouched on purpose: PortfolioSection and StatsSection have no framer at all
  and their GSAP already lives inside `mm.add("(min-width: 768px)")`;
  AboutSection is already fully `initial={false}` below md; the rotating-word and
  carousel-pagination transitions are not entry animations.
- Verified @1265px after reload at scroll 0 - every entry element still carries
  its initial inline style, i.e. desktop is untouched:
  hero h1 `opacity:0;filter:blur(6px);transform:translateY(28px)`,
  service/testimonial/contact/blog tags + footer link group
  `opacity:0;transform:translateY(20px)`, wordmark letter
  `transform:translateY(110%)`. `isMobile` resolves false at 1265, true at 390.
- LIMITATION: the Browser pane is not compositing (rAF probe: 0 frames in
  4530ms), so the mobile timing could not be observed in-pane. Structural proof
  only: `bunx next build` succeeds (every route prerendered, so SSR of the
  lazy-init hook is exercised), `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean, page renders fully at
  390px (8 service rows, 10 wordmark letters, no ReferenceError).
- Biome: no new diagnostics. ContactSection's `noUnusedVariables` on
  `GRID_COLUMNS` (line 44) is pre-existing - confirmed by stashing the file and
  re-running the lint.

## BlogSection - swap the mobile CTA for prev/next carousel arrows

- `src/components/ui/LogoCarousel.tsx`: `useMarqueeHalf` now RETURNS a stable
  `step(dx)` callback (held in a ref, so the identity survives re-renders while
  the effect swaps the implementation). Backward compatible - LogoCarousel and
  ExperimentalTestimonials ignore the return value and are untouched. Stepping
  reuses the drag path's exact machinery: cancel the WAAPI animation, write the
  current transform, transition to `originX + dx` over STEP_MS (500ms), then
  recreate the animation at the matching time. A transform transition is
  composited, so it never leaves the compositor. It travels to the UNWRAPPED
  target and wraps only on handoff - wrapping mid-transition would animate a
  whole copy-width slide.
- `src/components/home/BlogSection.tsx`: CTA wrapper `max-md:justify-start` ->
  `max-md:hidden`; added a `md:hidden` prev/next pair in the same header slot so
  the row does not reflow. Stride is MEASURED (`card.offsetWidth + marginRight`)
  rather than derived from 80vw. `active:` states, not `hover:` - touch has no
  hover.
- Direction note: the track animates -50% -> 0, i.e. content drifts RIGHT, so
  "next" is a NEGATIVE x step. Verified rather than assumed.
- Verified @390px: CTA `display: none`; both 48x48 arrows render; stride
  312 + 16 = 328px. Next -> wrappedDelta -328 (expected -328); Prev ->
  wrappedDelta +328 (expected +328) and `returnedToStart: true`. Raw deltas were
  +984/-984, i.e. the same position wrapped by the 1312px copy width - visually
  identical, which is the point of the two-copy track. During a step the track
  had 0 animations and inline `transform 500ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`;
  after, 1 animation restored with inline transform AND transition both cleared,

- No regression in the hook's other consumers: at 390px all four marquee tracks

## PortfolioSection - mobile carousel smoothness

- Root cause, measured not guessed: the tech-tag chips carry `backdrop-blur-md`,
  and the track held **19** elements computing `backdrop-filter: blur(12px)`
  inside the horizontal scroller. Every one of those makes the compositor
  snapshot and blur its backdrop on EVERY frame while swiping.
- Fix: `max-md:backdrop-blur-none` + `max-md:bg-black/50` on the chip (the
  heavier flat background keeps it legible over the photo without the blur).
  Desktop keeps `backdrop-blur-md` and `bg-black/20`.
- Verified @390px: elements in the track computing backdrop-filter or filter
  went 19 -> **0**; chip backdropFilter "none", background oklab(0 0 0 / 0.5).
- Verified @1265px unchanged: 19 chips still at blur(12px), bg 0.2, padding
  6px 16px, 12px text; track overflow-x visible, snap none, width 6325px (GSAP
  translates it there).
- Ruled out, so noting it so it is not re-investigated:
  * Lenis is NOT involved - SmoothScroll early-returns below 768px before
    constructing it, so no nested-scroller conflict.
  * The one <video> in the track was already paused offscreen (videosPlaying 0).
  * next/image already emits `decoding="async"` on all panel images, so there
    was nothing to gain there; `loading="eager"` was left alone deliberately -
    the existing comment explains lazy leaves black panels on a fast swipe.
  * The autoplay rAF tween writes scrollLeft for 600ms every 4500ms; left as is,
    since a scroll container cannot be advanced off the main thread and the
    prior attempt at `behavior:"smooth"` is documented as unreliable.
- LIMITATION: the Browser pane is not compositing (rAF frozen), so frame rate
  could not be measured in-pane. The claim here is the amount of per-frame work
  removed (19 backdrop-filter layers -> 0), not a measured FPS delta - confirm
  the feel on device.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean; `bunx next build` compiled; biome unchanged at the
  file's 2 pre-existing diagnostics.

## AboutSection - mobile image stacking animation

- NEW `src/components/home/AboutImageStack.tsx`; AboutSection's mobile branch
  swapped from a single static <Image> to `<AboutImageStack images={...} />`.
  The desktop framer/AnimatePresence stack is untouched.
- Three perf decisions, all following lessons already paid for this session:
  * The tick lives in the LEAF, not AboutSection. Ticking AboutSection's
    `frontIndex` would re-render the whole ~315-line section every few seconds
    to move three boxes — the exact trap TestimonialsRotatingWord was pulled
    out of.
  * Motion is CSS transitions on `transform` + `opacity` only, not a framer
    spring. Both are compositor properties, so the browser interpolates them
    with zero per-frame JS once the transition starts.
  * `will-change: transform, opacity` is STATIC, keeping the layers alive
    between cycles instead of rebuilding them on every swap.
- Off-screen gating is a SYNCHRONOUS getBoundingClientRect check at tick time,
  not an IntersectionObserver flag — an async flag that fails to arrive latches
  and kills the loop permanently, which is how the portfolio autoplay died.
  Also honours prefers-reduced-motion.
- `origin-top` is what makes it read as a stack: scaling about the top edge
  keeps it anchored so the negative y is the only lift, and each card's top
  peeks above the one in front by exactly that amount.
- Verified @390px geometry: 3 layers, z 3/2/1, transform-origin `183.2px 0px`,
  transitionProperty exactly `transform, opacity` (no layout properties),
  willChange `transform, opacity`. Slots: y0/scale1/op1/w366,
  y-16/scale.94/op.85/w344, y-30/scale.88/op.7/w322 — i.e. 16px and 30px peeks.
- Verified the cycle RUNS: scrolled into view and sampled 19.2s — z-order
  rotated 3/2/1 -> 1/3/2 -> 2/1/3 -> 3/2/1 across 6 transitions at ~3.4-3.6s
  (3500ms hold, background-tab timer clamping explains the drift). Every card
  visits every slot.
- Verified the off-screen gate HOLDS: scrolled to top, 65.7s elapsed = 18
  possible ticks, z-order unchanged 1/3/2 -> 1/3/2 (`stayedPut: true`).
- Verified @1266px untouched: the perspective box still holds the framer cards
  directly (`origin-bottom-right`, transitionProperty `all`),
  `usesMobileStackHost: false` — AboutImageStack does not mount on desktop.
- LIMITATION: the pane does not composite (rAF frozen), so smoothness could not
  be measured as FPS. The claim here is structural — compositor-only properties,
  no per-frame JS, no section-wide re-render — not a measured frame rate.
  Confirm the feel on device.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean; `bunx next build` compiled; biome 0 diagnostics on
  AboutImageStack, AboutSection unchanged at its 1 pre-existing noArrayIndexKey.

## About page - mobile responsiveness (plan at .claude/plan.md)

### P0 found by audit, not by eye
The two scroll-overlap groups hard-coded DESKTOP heights in their sticky
offsets: `top-[calc(100vh-1104px)]` and `top-[calc(100vh-994px)]`. At 390px the
real heights are 1253px and 1437px, so the pinned blocks overflowed the fold by
149px and 443px. Measured consequence at scrollY 900:
`statsRowTop: 624` vs `nextSectionTop: 353`, `statsClippedByNextSection: true`
- the entire hero stats row (10+/250+/98%/40+) rendered UNDERNEATH the black
section and was never visible on mobile. Content loss, not just spacing.

Root cause vs the homepage: only `ShrinkOnOverlap`'s GSAP was md-gated; the
sticky + negative-margin rig around it was not. The homepage gates the whole rig
(`md:-mt-[100vh]`, pin inside `min-width:768px`). Ported that.

### Changes (5 files, all `max-md:`/base-value scoped)

## Homepage navbar - mobile smoothness

### What I ruled out first (so it is not re-investigated)
- `transition-property: all` on the header row is NOT a global rule - it is the
  CSS initial value. A freshly created plain div reports the same `all` / `0s`.
- The two `filter: blur(40px)` / `blur(24px)` elements inside the nav subtree
  belong to the desktop DynamicButton, which sits under `display: none` at
  mobile width, so they cost nothing there.
- Nav subtree is 50 elements on mobile, 41 of them the `display:none` desktop
  tree. It is reconciled on `visible`/`isHidden` flips - a few times per scroll
  session, NOT per frame - so it is not the lag source. Left mounted; unmounting
  it needs a JS viewport check and would risk hydration.

### The actual cause
`backdrop-blur-2xl` = `blur(40px)` on the floating bar. A backdrop-filter over
the hero's AUTOPLAYING video has to re-sample and re-blur its backdrop on every
video frame, not just when the bar moves - so it was continuous GPU work the
whole time the bar floated over the hero. This is exactly what the pre-existing
comment in this file warned about when it chose an opaque bar; I reintroduced
the blur two tasks ago at explicit request and flagged it then.

### Changes (mobile dropdown branch only)
- `backdrop-blur-2xl` -> `backdrop-blur-md` (40px -> **12px**) with the
  background raised `/70` -> `/90` so it still reads as one solid dark bar.
  Verified: `backdropFilter: "blur(12px)"`, `background: lab(.../0.9)`,
  `isPureBlack: false`.
- Shell transition 300ms -> **200ms**. `width` is a layout property and every
  layout tick also forces the backdrop to be re-sampled at the new geometry, so
  the shorter window compounds with the smaller radius. Verified
  `transitionDuration: "0.2s"`.
- `setIsHidden` was called on EVERY scroll frame while scrolling down past
  120px. Replaced the if/else with the same functional guard `visible` already
  used one line above: `setIsHidden(prev => prev === shouldHide ? prev : shouldHide)`.
  Behaviour-identical, one fewer scheduled update per scroll frame.

### Verification
- @390 floating (forced): blur(12px), bg lab(.../0.9), radius 18px.
- @390 OPEN: blur(12px), width 96%, radius 18px, translate 0px 10px, 5 rows at
  20px, panel present - the feature set from the previous tasks is intact.
- @1265 desktop UNCHANGED: NavBody fixed, 1250px, padding 32/40, backdrop none,
  bg transparent; mobile shell `display: none`. The desktop bar's own
  `bg-black/60 backdrop-blur-2xl` is untouched (still at line 141).
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean; `bunx next build` compiled + 35/35 pages; biome 12
  diagnostics (unchanged).

## Mobile heat/lag - hero video (plan at .claude/plan.md)

### Cause, measured
`public/assets/video7.mp4`, the autoplaying hero background, was
**3840x2160 HEVC at 16,670 kbps, 20 MB for 10s**. It is only ever shown two
ways, neither of which can use that: full-screen under `filter: blur(24px)`
(detail destroyed), and a 220px CSS canvas chip whose backing store is 275-440px.
Useful ceiling ~660 device px; it shipped 3840. On a phone that is a 20 MB
download plus continuous 4K HEVC decode - and where there is no HEVC hardware
path the browser falls back to SOFTWARE 4K decode, which alone pegs the CPU.
Every other video in the project is already H.264 <= 5 Mbps; this was the
outlier by 8x.

### Changes
1. Re-encoded to **1280x720 H.264, 1,103 kbps** (lanczos downscale, `-movflags
   +faststart`, audio dropped - the element is `muted` with no controls).
   **20,436 KB -> 1,356 KB (-93.4%)**, and 720p H.264 hardware-decodes on every
   phone. Original kept at `public/assets/video7.mp4.orig` pending sign-off.
2. `Herosection.tsx` canvas loop: rAF -> `requestVideoFrameCallback` with an rAF
   fallback. rVFC fires once per PRESENTED VIDEO frame (24fps here); rAF fired
   once per DISPLAY refresh (60-120fps on a phone), so the loop was re-copying
   the same decoded frame 3-5x over. The existing cancel-then-restart contract
   on `play` is preserved (VideoViewportPause pauses/resumes it offscreen).

### Two type errors hit and fixed en route
- `function drawFrame()` is hoisted, which drops TS's null-narrowing of
  video/canvas/ctx -> 6 errors. Arrow consts restore it; `drawFrame` may
  reference `schedule` before its declaration since it is not *called* until
  both exist.
- `HTMLVideoElement & Partial<Pick<...>>` does NOT make the rVFC methods
  optional - intersecting a required property with an optional one yields
  required, so TS2774 "always defined". Cast through `unknown` instead.

### Verification
- Asset: BEFORE `hevc,3840,2160` / 20,436 KB -> AFTER `h264,1280,720` /
  1,356 KB. Same duration 10.04s, same 241 frames, same 24fps.
- NO UI CHANGE, checked structurally: the JSX diff contains zero
  `className`/`<video>`/`<canvas>` lines ("NONE - no JSX/className lines
  touched"). At 390px and 1266px the video still computes
  `className: "absolute inset-0 w-full h-full object-cover scale-110 blur-xl"`,
  `filter: blur(24px)`, `scale: 1.1`, `object-fit: cover` - identical to before.
- Runtime: `intrinsicResolution 1280x720`, `readyState 4`,
  `rvfcSupported: true`, video served 206 Partial Content, no new console errors.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean; `bunx next build` compiled + 35/35 pages; biome
  identical before and after (2 pre-existing on line 13).

### LIMITATION
The pane does not composite (rAF frozen), so the canvas repaint could not be
observed and no FPS/thermal delta was measured. The claims here are the work
removed - 93.4% fewer bytes, 4K HEVC -> 720p H.264 decode, ~3-5x fewer canvas
uploads - not a measured frame rate. Re-test on the phone.

### Still open, deliberately
- `filter: blur(24px)` on the full-screen video still re-blurs every decoded
  frame. Baking the blur into the asset would remove that entirely and is
  probably the largest remaining win, but the radius must be matched by eye
  across viewports and I cannot verify appearance here - it is a UI risk and the
  task said no UI change. Best next step IF the phone still runs warm.
- `public/assets` is still ~58 MB after this, with 8 images over 1.5 MB (largest
  2.9 MB) and video1.mp4 at 10 MB / 4,968 kbps on the About page.

### Routing
Planned 3/3 steps `driver` and flagged that at the gate rather than padding to
hit the <=20% budget: step 1 is one ffmpeg call whose only real content is
choosing the ladder, step 2 is ~15 lines in one file that must preserve an
existing cleanup contract. User approved. No workers dispatched, so no
spec-verifier gate (T1 restraint).

## Mobile perf - profiled DEV vs PRODUCTION (headline finding)

### The number that explains it
Same page, same viewport (390px), measured via Resource Timing:

| | dev `next dev` :3000 | prod `next start` :3100 |
|---|---|---|
| **JS** | **21.22 MB** | **0.96 MB** |
| total | 24.78 MB | 4.45 MB |
| requests | 38 | 20 |

**Production JS is 22x smaller.** The dev bloat is entirely react-icons barrel
imports: `/si` 6,309 KB, `/md` 4,525 KB, `/ri` 3,220 KB, `/fa` 1,930 KB =
**15,991 KB** for **43 distinct icons** actually used. Turbopack dev does not
tree-shake barrels; the production build already does.

If the phone is pointed at `next dev` over LAN, that is 21 MB of unminified JS
to download, parse and execute — which is exactly "very slow, heats up, laggy in
every animation". Nothing in the app code causes it.

### Two fixes attempted and REVERTED because they measurably did nothing
1. `experimental.optimizePackageImports` for react-icons/tabler/lucide.
   After: dev JS still **21.22 MB**, icon chunks still **15,991 KB**, still
   named `node_modules_react-icons_si_index_mjs_*` (whole barrel). Production
   bundle byte-identical: **4323 KB with and without**. Complete no-op under
   Turbopack — reverted rather than left as dead config.
2. `preload="none"` on PortfolioSection's video. After: element still reported
   `preload: "metadata"`, `readyState: 4`, **1,898 KB still fetched**. Per spec
   `autoPlay` overrides `preload`, so the attribute cannot work there —
   reverted.

### Production runtime is actually healthy
1620 DOM nodes, 4 animations (2 running), **zero** rendered backdrop-filters,
0.96 MB JS. This does not look like a laggy page.

### Real remaining production costs, measured, NOT changed
- Hero `filter: blur(24px)` full-screen over the autoplaying video —
  `rendered: true`, continuous GPU work per decoded frame. Still the largest
  single cost. Removing it needs the blur baked into the asset, which I cannot
  verify visually in this pane (it does not composite) and the task says the UI
  must stay identical. Needs a go-ahead.
- `video3.mp4` **1,898 KB** downloads and decodes on load for a panel that is
  thousands of px below the fold. `preload` cannot fix it (see above); the real
  fix is to mount the `<video>` only when the panel nears the viewport, which
  means new IO state inside PortfolioSection's already-delicate mobile autoplay
  logic. Deliberately not done unprompted.
- `blur(64px)` decorative blob in AboutSection and a `drop-shadow(0 10px 40px)`
  on the footer wordmark — one-time paints, minor.

### Net diff from this task: NONE
Both experiments were reverted after measurement. The deliverable is the
dev-vs-prod evidence, not a code change.

## Hero blur: blur a quarter-size surface instead of the full screen

User confirmed they test a DEPLOYED build, so production is what they feel -
the dev-vs-prod finding in the previous entry is NOT the explanation for them.

### Why the asset was NOT pre-blurred (the approved approach, rejected on evidence)
`object-cover` means one source pixel covers a different number of CSS pixels at
every viewport, so the sigma a baked file would need is not constant:

| viewport | cover scale | sigma the asset would need |
|---|---|---|
| 390x844 | 1.172 | 20.5 |
| 393x852 | 1.183 | 20.3 |
| 768x1024 | 1.422 | 16.9 |
| 1266x900 | 1.250 | 19.2 |
| 1920x1080 | 1.500 | 16.0 |

A 28% spread. Tuning for the phone would leave desktop ~28% over-blurred, which
breaks the standing "never change desktop" rule.

### What was done instead
Blur a QUARTER-SIZE surface and scale it back up. Gaussian sigma scales with the
transform, so `blur(6px) x scale(4.4)` is EXACTLY the previous
`blur(24px) x scale(1.1)` = 26.4 on screen, at every viewport, with no asset
change and instant revert.

`<video class="absolute inset-0 w-full h-full object-cover scale-110 blur-xl">`
becomes a wrapper `absolute inset-0 overflow-hidden` around
`absolute left-[-5%] top-[-5%] h-[25%] w-[25%] origin-top-left scale-[4.4]
object-cover blur-[6px]`. left/top -5% reproduce what the centred `scale-110`
did (a centred 110% scale puts the top-left at -5% of the box). The 25% box has
the same aspect ratio as the parent, so `object-cover` crops identically.

### Verified in PRODUCTION (`next start`), both breakpoints
| | 390x844 | 1266x900 |
|---|---|---|
| effective on-screen sigma | **26.4** | **26.4** |
| previous sigma | 26.4 | 26.4 |
| `sigmaMatchesExactly` | **true** | **true** |
| painted box | 403x891 | 1349x955 |
| expected painted box | 403x891 | 1349x955 |
| `coversHero` | true | true |
| pixels blurred per frame | **18,554** (was 296,871) | **66,571** (was 1,065,128) |
| reduction | 16x | **16x** |

So: 16x fewer pixels blurred, each with a 4x smaller kernel, on every decoded
frame of an autoplaying video. Painted geometry is byte-identical to before.

### A measurement error I made and corrected
`pkill -f "next start"` does not match the Next process on Windows. Three
"production" restarts silently failed with EADDRINUSE (found in the log only
after the served HTML kept showing old classes) while the ORIGINAL server kept
answering curl with 200. Every prod measurement between the first one and this
fix was therefore against a stale build. Killed PID 19092 via `Stop-Process`
and re-measured; the numbers above are from a confirmed-fresh server
(`curl | grep scale-[4.4]` returns a hit before measuring).

Consequence: the earlier claim that `preload="none"` on PortfolioSection's video
"measurably did nothing" was based on that stale server and is NOT evidence. The
spec reasoning still holds (`autoplay` forces the browser to load regardless of
`preload`), but it was not actually verified. It remains reverted and untested.

### Net diff: 1 file, Herosection.tsx (+23/-9)
`bunx tsc --noEmit` clean; `bunx next build` compiled; biome unchanged (2
pre-existing on line 13). optimizePackageImports and preload="none" both
confirmed still reverted (0 refs each).

### Still open
- `video3.mp4` 1,898 KB downloads and decodes on load for a below-the-fold
  panel. Real fix is mounting the `<video>` only when the panel nears the
  viewport.
- `public/assets` ~58 MB, 8 images over 1.5 MB.

## Homepage - genuinely remove mobile entrance animations

### Why the earlier NO_ENTRY pass was not enough
`transition={isMobile ? NO_ENTRY : ...}` only made the animation INSTANT. The
elements still rendered at `initial` (opacity 0) and only reached opacity 1 when
`whileInView` fired, so content still popped in on scroll — and worse, the SSR
HTML shipped them at opacity 0, so the page was largely blank until React
hydrated. Measured in production at 390px BEFORE this change: **27 elements
sitting at opacity 0** at scroll top (hero copy, services, testimonials, ...).

### Approach chosen, and the two rejected
Gating `initial` on `useIsMobile()` was the obvious fix and was rejected: the
hook returns false on the server and true on the first client render, so the
emitted `style` attribute would differ and hydration would mismatch.
Pre-computing it server-side is impossible — the server has no viewport.

Done in CSS instead. `src/app/globals.css`:

```
@media not (min-width: 48rem) {
  [data-no-mobile-entry] {
    opacity: 1 !important; transform: none !important;
    translate: none !important; filter: none !important;
  }
}
```

framer writes `initial` as an INLINE style, so `!important` is required to win.
Two properties of doing it this way matter: it needs no hydration, so the
content is visible in the FIRST PAINT rather than waiting for React; and SSR and
client render identical markup, so there is no mismatch. The inline
`opacity:0;...` is deliberately left in place and simply overridden.

`data-no-mobile-entry` added to the 23 entrance `motion` elements across
Herosection (6), ServiceSection (3), ExperimentalTestimonials (4),
ContactSection (3), BlogSection (3), Footer (4). The 2
`initial={{ x: "-100%" }}` props were deliberately NOT tagged — those are the
rotating-word swaps, not entrances.

### Verified in PRODUCTION (`next start`, confirmed-fresh server)
- @390px: 25 tagged DOM elements (23 source tags; Footer's link-group map
  renders one of them 3x). `stillTransparent: 0`, `stillFiltered: 0`,
  all transforms identity, **`allNeutralised: true`**. Sweep for any visible
  element left at opacity 0 returns 8, all of them `pointer-events-none`
  hover overlays (`opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100`) — not entrances.
  `ruleInStylesheet: true`, so it applies before any JS runs.
- @1266px: `mediaQueryMatchesAtThisWidth: false`,
  `elementsStillAtInitialState: 25` (opacity 0, translateY(28px)) — the desktop
  entrances are completely untouched.
- No hydration errors in the console (only pre-existing 404s).

### A correction to my own reading mid-task
I first reported "24 still translated". That predicate compared against the
string `'none'`; the computed value was `matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0)` — the
IDENTITY matrix, i.e. no offset. The CSS was working; the check was wrong.

### Housekeeping
`biome format --write src/components/home/*.tsx` re-wrapped one unrelated line
in PortfolioSection.tsx. Reverted via `git checkout` after confirming that file
carries none of this task's tags.

Net diff: 7 files, +39 lines, no deletions. `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean;
`bunx next build` compiled; biome 8 diagnostics across the six components, all
pre-existing.

### Note
The `isMobile ? NO_ENTRY : ...` transitions on these 23 elements are now
redundant — the CSS overrides the visual result regardless. Left in place rather
than making 23 more edits for no functional gain.

## Mobile smoothness - compositor layers + second video

### Measured cause: 12 permanently-promoted layers, most of which never move
At 390px the page held **12 compositor layers totalling 1,526,970 px**, and the
three biggest were `will-change: transform` on elements that are ONLY ever
transformed by ScrollTrigger inside `mm.add("(min-width: 768px)")` — i.e. never
on a phone:

| element | box | transformed on mobile |
|---|---|---|
| testimonials wrapper (`page.tsx`) | 390x1126 = 439,091 px | no |
| about wrapper (`page.tsx`) | 390x974 = 379,903 px | no |
| `.stat-inner` x4 (`StatsSection`) | 390x153 each = 238,972 px | no |

~1.06M CSS px of GPU texture (≈9.5M device px at DPR 3) held for nothing, plus
the extra layers for the compositor to manage every frame — which is the shape
of "everything feels laggy" on a phone.

### Changes
1. Those three `will-change-transform` -> `md:will-change-transform`
   (`src/app/home/page.tsx` x2, `src/components/home/StatsSection.tsx` x1).
   The transform is desktop-only, so the hint should be too.
2. `public/assets/video3.mp4` re-encoded **1920x1080 -> 1280x720**, 1,900 KB ->
   **952 KB**. It plays inside a 390px-wide phone carousel panel (1170 device px
   at DPR 3), so 1080p was oversized — decoding a 1080p stream while that
   carousel is dragged/autoplayed is directly the "carousels are laggy"
   complaint. Original kept at `video3.mp4.orig`.

### Verified in PRODUCTION (`next start`, confirmed-fresh server each time)
- @390px: layers **12 -> 6**, promoted area **1,526,970 -> 469,004 px (-69%)**.
  The 4 remaining with non-zero area all genuinely animate (3 AboutImageStack
  slots + the LogoLoop marquee track).
- @390px videos: both now `1280x720`; total video bytes 3,251 -> **2,304 KB**.
- @1265px UNCHANGED: 15 promoted layers, both GSAP wrappers still promoted
  (1250x1030 and 1250x840, `willChange: transform`) and all 4 `.stat-inner`
  still promoted — the desktop pin still gets its hint.

### Honest limits on what this proves
- Main-thread scroll cost moved only 2.13 -> 2.03 ms per scroll step (-5%). The
  layer fix is a GPU-memory/compositing win, NOT a main-thread win, and this
  pane cannot measure GPU or frame rate. The 2.0 ms/step that remains is scroll
  listeners plus layout on a 1621-node DOM.
- I could not attribute that remaining cost: GSAP is bundled rather than on
  `window`, so `ScrollTrigger.getAll()` was unreachable and I could not A/B it.
- Not changed, still suspected: framer's `useScroll` in `Navbar` runs a callback
  on every scroll frame, and the 41-element desktop nav tree stays mounted and
  is reconciled on every scroll-direction change. Unmounting it below `lg` needs
  a viewport hook, which would desync SSR — deliberately not done unprompted.
- `BlogSection` calls `useAnimationFrame` unconditionally; the body early-returns
  on mobile but the callback still keeps framer's frame loop alive every frame.
  Fixing it means moving the desktop marquee into a desktop-only child.

`bunx tsc --noEmit` clean; `bunx next build` compiled; biome unchanged

## Mobile drag lag - the paused-marquee layer regression

### A theory disproven before any edit
Suspected the classic inline-component footgun: `CardTrack` is defined inside
BlogSection, so every 6s `setIndex` re-render should change its identity and
remount all 8 cards. Tested empirically in prod (branded the live DOM node,
waited past a tick): **node identity survived** - `reactCompiler: true`
auto-memoizes the inner component. No remount. Theory dropped, not fixed.

### The real mechanism (and it was MY regression)
When blog/testimonials went arrows-only, their WAAPI marquees became permanently
**paused** - and a paused animation drops off the compositor. Measured at rest:
both draggable tracks `willChange: auto`, animation `paused`, sizes 2627x453 and
2547x360. So the ~2600px track had NO layer at rest, and every pointerdown
re-rasterised it synchronously under the finger; the hook then cleared
`will-change` on release, guaranteeing the same stall on the NEXT drag. When the
marquee autoplayed (before the arrows change), the running animation kept the
layer alive - which is why drag used to feel better.

### Changes
1. `useMarqueeHalf` (LogoCarousel.tsx): draggable tracks are promoted
   STATICALLY for the hook's lifetime (`el.style.willChange = "transform"` at
   drag-section setup); removed all four per-drag/per-step set/clear writes.
   Cleanup still resets it. Non-draggable path (LogoLoop) untouched.
   Rasterisation is tiled, so the resident cost is visible tiles, not the whole
   strip.
2. BlogSection rotating-word interval gated to desktop - mobile renders
   `rotatingWords[0]` statically, so the tick only re-rendered the section every
   6s for nothing.
3. BlogSection `useAnimationFrame` moved into a `DesktopAutoScroll` child that
   mounts only when `isDesktop` - the unconditional hook kept framer's global
   frame loop alive at display refresh rate on mobile for a body that
   early-returned. The child renders null, so conditional mounting cannot
   desync SSR.

### Verified in PRODUCTION
- @390: both draggable tracks now `willChange: transform` at rest with anims
  `paused`; arrows still step exactly (blog -328, testimonials -318, wrapped);
  promotion survives a step (`willChangeAfterStep: "transform"`).
  LogoLoop/TechLogoCarousel running as before.
- @1266: tracks back to `willChange: auto` (hook disabled there), 0 WAAPI anims,
  and the track carries a framer-written `translateX(-1314px)` - proof
  DesktopAutoScroll mounted and IS driving the desktop marquee post-refactor.
  Desktop rotating word still animated.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean; build compiled; biome count unchanged at 1
  (the pre-existing useExhaustiveDependencies, moved 98 -> 127 by added lines).

### Why this wasn't caught earlier + the standing caveat
Every pass so far attacked continuous costs (blur, video decode, layers, frame
loops); drag START cost only exists at the moment of pointerdown and cannot be
felt in a pane whose rAF is frozen. Same limitation still holds - no FPS/thermal
measurement here, claims are mechanism-level. ALSO worth saying: all fixes are
in the PRODUCTION build (`next start`); if the phone is testing `bun run dev`,
dev-mode overhead will mask every one of these wins.

## "Still laggy" - the phone is testing the wrong server

No code change this round; the finding is about what is being measured.

- Two servers are live, both bound 0.0.0.0: **:3000 = `npm run dev`** (what the
  session previews used all along, and almost certainly what the phone opens)
  and **:3100 = `next start`** on the current build (where every perf fix was
  verified).
- Yesterday's commit (aa85e00, pushed) predates today's drag fixes -
  BlogSection/LogoCarousel changes are uncommitted, so any DEPLOYED url has
  none of them either.
- Measured the difference in-pane at 390px, same route:

  | server | scripts | total JS |
  |---|---|---|
  | dev :3000 | 29 | **21,735 KB** |
  | prod :3100 | 11 | **987 KB** |

  **22x more JavaScript in dev.** On this desktop-class machine the scroll-step
  cost is equal (1.44 vs 1.53 ms - parse is done, machine is fast), but a phone
  must download, parse and run those 21.7 MB with the React dev runtime's
  checks on every interaction - drag included. No optimisation can make dev
  mode feel smooth on a phone.
- Prod verified reachable on the LAN at **http://192.168.29.24:3100/home**
  (200, 311 KB HTML) and serving the fixed build (6x md:will-change-transform
  markers). No firewall block rule on node; :3000 works from the phone via the
  identical binding, so :3100 should too.
- ACTION FOR USER: open http://192.168.29.24:3100/home on the phone and judge
  smoothness THERE. If that is smooth, the site is fixed and the remaining gap
  was dev mode. If it is still laggy on :3100, that is a real signal worth the
  next investigation round.

## Blog + Testimonials carousels -> native scroll-snap (mobile)

### The decision
User narrowed the complaint to exactly the two carousels still driven by JS
pointer events; PortfolioSection - native scroll-snap - was implicitly certified
smooth. JS pointermove dragging pays main-thread latency by construction (events
delivered on the main thread, transform written a frame later, blocked by any
script); native scrolling runs on the compositor thread and cannot be blocked.
After three rounds of micro-optimising the JS path, the correct fix was to stop
using it: both carousels now use Portfolio's mechanics below md.

### Changes
- NEW `src/lib/tweenScrollLeft.ts`: Portfolio's proven snap-safe arrow tween
  (programmatic smooth scroll is unreliable against `snap-mandatory`; disable
  snap for the tween, restore to land).
- `ExperimentalTestimonials.tsx` / `BlogSection.tsx` below md:
  * wrapper -> `max-md:overflow-x-auto max-md:snap-x max-md:snap-mandatory
    max-md:overscroll-x-contain no-scrollbar` (blog keeps `scroll-pl-3`;
    testimonials cards `snap-center`, track `px-11` so edge cards can centre;
    blog cards `snap-start`)
  * `useMarqueeHalf` calls REMOVED (no WAAPI, no JS drag, no step machinery);
    arrows now tween the scroller with wrap-at-ends
  * the second list copy - which existed only for the -50% wrap - is CSS-hidden
    below md (`max-md:hidden`), so SSR markup is identical at both breakpoints
- Hook itself untouched; its one remaining consumer is LogoLoop
  (TechLogoCarousel wraps LogoCarousel's default export).
- BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, disclosed: mobile drag is now FINITE (4 cards, ends stop)
  instead of infinitely wrapping. Arrows wrap: next at the last card returns to
  the start. Visuals at rest are identical.

- Cause: RotatingWord's GRADIENT span carries `px-2` so the DESKTOP slide
  animation's glyphs clear the wrapper's overflow-hidden. On mobile the word is
  static, so the uncancelled 8px of left padding stacked on the h1's 10px flex
  gap: "founders" sat 18px from "for" while every other pair sat at 10px.

  branch ever renders (isDesktop is false there), so the animated version cannot
  be affected by construction.

  WRAPPER (its motion.span ancestor is also a span - descendant selectors look
  at ancestry, not :scope), which reported a nonsense -14. Re-measured against

## PortfolioSection - compositor card transition (mobile)

### Cause
The finger-drag is native scroll (smooth); the laggy "transition between the
cards" was the AUTOPLAY slide - a rAF loop writing `track.scrollLeft` every
frame for 600ms. scrollLeft can only be driven from the main thread, so the
slide stuttered whenever anything else ran during its window.

### Fix
- New inner wrapper (`panelsRef`, `flex w-full flex-row md:contents`) around
  all six panels. Below md it is the slide surface; on md `display: contents`
  erases the box so GSAP keeps translating the track exactly as before.
- `animateTo` now runs a CSS `transform` transition on that wrapper
  (600ms, cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1) = the old easeInOutCubic), then COMMITS
  the distance to scrollLeft in the same style flush that clears the transform
  - an invisible swap. Snap disabled during, restored after, as before.
- Commit hardening after an in-pane diagnostic: on COMPLETION commit the
  slide's own intended distance (works even if the transition was throttled -
  background tabs coalesce transitions but the intent is known); only an
  INTERRUPTION (stopTween) measures the computed matrix mid-flight.
- The old rAF-reclaim dance in advance() deleted - setTimeout always fires,
  so `sliding` cannot wedge shut.
- Desktop panelCount switched to `querySelectorAll(".project-panel")` - the
  wrapper made `track.children.length` = 1.

### Diagnostics worth keeping
- This pane CANNOT run CSS transitions at all: computed transform stays at the
  START value even past the transition's end (verified: inline transform with
  no transition reads -390; with a 100ms transition it reads identity forever).
  First commit version measured the matrix at timeout and therefore committed
  0 in-pane; target-distance commit is immune and also strictly better in real
  browsers.

### Verified in PROD @390
scrollLeft progression across five autoplay ticks:
**0 -> 390 -> 780 -> 1170 -> 1560 -> 1952** (= track max, 2342-390), exactly
one page per 4.5s tick; wrapper transform cleared and snap restored after
every slide (samples show `translate3d(-390px)` + snap `none` DURING, cleared +
default AFTER, every cycle).

### Verified @1265
wrapper `display: contents`, no inline styles; 6 panels found; track 7590 =
6x1265; pin-spacer 8125 = 900+6325+900 (viewport-rounding of the earlier 8128);
first project's reveal still armed at opacity 0. Desktop untouched.

## AboutSection - mobile stack got a real exit phase

### Cause (a defect in my own earlier implementation)
The mobile stack cycled by rotating SLOT poses and flipping z-index. z-index is
discrete, so at each swap the front card jumped BEHIND the other two in a single
frame while its 700ms transform tween then played out hidden. Nothing was
dropping frames — the motion was simply invisible, which reads as a pop. The
desktop version never had this because AnimatePresence gives its exiting card a
real exit (x 1000 / y 400 / rotateZ 90).

### Fix
- New `EXIT` pose (y 56, scale 0.92, opacity 0) and a `leaving` index kept
  SEPARATE from `front`, so promoting the other cards is not delayed by the
  exit.
- The leaver holds the TOP z-index for its whole exit — it is now seen leaving
  rather than cut behind the stack — then a timer (not `transitionend`, which
  can be dropped and would strand the card invisible) clears `leaving`.
- The card returning to the deepest slot does so with `transition: none`, so
  the audience never sees it travel back up.
- Still transform + opacity only, `will-change` still static: the exit adds
  zero new work for the compositor.

### Verified in PROD @390, 108.9s / 63 state changes
Every cycle shows the same clean two-phase shape, e.g.
`z4 op0 s0.92 anim` (leaver on top, fading out) -> ~710ms later
`z1 op0.7 s0.88 none` (silently reseated at the back).
Across ~30 swaps the exit pose appears EXACTLY once per cycle and always at
z4 (above the 3-card stack); no cycle skipped, none stuck invisible. Roles
rotate 0->1->2->0 with no drift over the whole run.

### Verified @1266
`usesMobileHost: false`, 6 direct framer children with `origin-bottom-right`,
transitionProperty `all`, and `hasExitPoseAnywhere: false` — the mobile EXIT
pose never renders on desktop. Untouched.

tsc clean, build compiled, biome 0 diagnostics on the file.

## Blog + Testimonials - infinite mobile carousels

- NEW `src/lib/useInfiniteCarousel.ts`. Track renders 3 identical runs on
  mobile; scrolling PARKS in run 2, so there is a full run of runway either
  way. When the position comes within one slide of a true end, scrollLeft jumps
  exactly one run - invisible (runs are pixel-identical) and lands on the same
  snap boundary, so the snap engine does not re-animate.
- Wrapping at the EXTREMES, not the middle: assigning scrollLeft during an iOS
  momentum fling kills the fling, and the extremes are where a fling has
  already run out. Same cancel-and-rearm rAF guard as CarouselDots (a
  "one pending" flag latches if its callback never runs).
- Run width is `slideStride * itemCount` measured from `[data-slide]` offsets,
  NOT `scrollWidth / copies` - both tracks carry their own horizontal padding
  (testimonials centres with `px-11`, blog `px-3`), which would skew a
  scrollWidth ratio and let the modular arithmetic drift.
- CarouselDots gained `loop`: active index is now `round(scrollLeft/stride) %
  count` while looping (a ratio against full scrollWidth would sweep the dots
  three times per lap), and tapping a dot steps to the NEAREST occurrence of
  that slide rather than its absolute index, so it never rewinds a whole lap.
- Copy counts arranged so DESKTOP IS BYTE-IDENTICAL: testimonials array tripled
  with run 3 `md:hidden`; blog gains two `md:hidden` CardTracks alongside the
  existing `max-md:hidden` one. Desktop sees exactly 2 runs either way, which
  its framer wrap depends on.

## PortfolioSection - CtaSection's SpotlightGrid on the title slide (mobile)

- The "auto moving animation" in CtaSection is `SpotlightGrid` (a scattered
  sweep of glowing cells). Mounted it in the title slide's masked layer with

  sweepColStart 2, sweepRowStart 2, sweepRowEnd 5), replacing the static cells

  mode supplies no mask of its own, so the wrapper is what gives the falloff.
- PERF GATE, and why it exists: SpotlightGrid runs a permanent rAF loop and is
  not otherwise on the homepage, so mounting it unconditionally would add
  per-frame work that keeps running while the user is anywhere else on the page
  — the exact cost this section has been stripped of. It now mounts only while
  the slide is within 200px of the viewport.
- The gate is a POLLED rect read (400ms interval), not an IntersectionObserver.
  First attempt used framer's `useInView`; it never mounted, because IO
  callbacks are delivered during rendering steps that this pane has frozen —
  and more importantly that is the async-flag pattern which has already killed
  this very section's autoplay once. A polled rect read cannot latch.

- Gate verified BOTH ways: scrolled to top it unmounts (sampled every 300ms:
  mounted through 3130ms, `mounted: false` from 4141ms on — this pane throttles
  background timers, so the 400ms poll fires far slower here than on device),

## PortfolioSection - title slide holds 10s, others 5s (mobile)

- This is now genuinely TWO values, where the previous request read as a uniform
  5s. New `MOBILE_FIRST_SLIDE_MS = 10000` alongside `MOBILE_AUTOPLAY_MS = 5000`.
- The interval still fires every 5s; a `lastAdvance` timestamp plus a per-slide
  `hold` lets slide 0 sit for two ticks while every other slide advances on the
  first. Slide index is read from `scrollLeft` AT TICK TIME (synchronous) rather
  than tracked in a counter, so a drag or a dot tap cannot desync it — the same
  rule the rest of this effect already follows.
- `lastAdvance` is also reset while the reader is interacting and while the
  section is off screen, so a slide always gets its full hold from the moment it
  is actually visible and unbothered, rather than firing the instant a gate
  lapses. 50ms tolerance absorbs setInterval drift (an elapsed of 9998 against a
  10000 hold would otherwise cost a whole extra tick).
- Desktop's `AUTO_ADVANCE_SECONDS = 6` untouched.

### Verification, and an important caveat about this pane
- Subsequent slides: gaps **[4997, 5006, 4996, 5001] ms** across a clean run —
  5s to within 6ms.
- Slide 0: held **9002ms** measured from a sample start that was UP TO 1s after
  the real dwell began (the dwell starts at the prior interval tick, which is
  not observable), so the true hold is ~10s. It is unambiguously ~2x the others.
- Apparent "stalls" mid-testing were NOT a regression: a direct probe measured
  **6 timer ticks in 5621ms where 22 were expected — this pane throttles timers
  ~4x**, which stretches a 5s interval to ~20s. Confirmed live at the same
  moment: scrollLeft had advanced 390 -> 780 with the panels wrapper caught
  mid-slide (`translate3d(-390px)`, 600ms transition active). Autoplay is
  healthy; only the pane's clock is slow.
- @1265: track `overflow-x: visible`, scrollLeft 0, scrollWidth 7590, 6 panels,
  pin-spacer 8125 — GSAP-pinned, neither hold constant runs there.
- tsc clean, build compiled, biome at the file's baseline 2.

## Navbar - framer taken off the scroll path (both copies)

### The answer to "why is it still laggy, especially the navbar"
The video was never the navbar's problem. THREE things ran on every scroll:
1. `useScroll` + `useMotionValueEvent` — framer library code per scroll frame,
   only to produce two booleans.
2. `setIsHidden` state — flipping on every scroll DIRECTION CHANGE re-rendered
   Navbar, and each render re-runs its `React.Children.map` + `cloneElement`
   pass over the ENTIRE nav subtree (~50 elements, the display:none desktop
   tree included). On a phone, momentum scrolling reverses constantly.
3. The hide/show slide was a framer spring = per-frame JS.

### Changes (both files, identical treatment)
- `src/components/ui/resizable-navbar.tsx` (homepage) and
  `src/components/page/resizable-navbar.tsx` (every other route — a full copy
  of the same component, which is why fixing only one would have left most of
  the site slow; its `setIsHidden` was still UNGUARDED, firing every frame).
- Scroll handling is now a native `{ passive: true }` listener. Hide/show is a
  DIRECT `el.style.translate` write plus `transition-[translate] duration-300
  ease-out` — same 300ms ease-out, run by the compositor, and it no longer
  touches React at all. `visible` remains state (children restyle from it) but
  flips only when the 80px threshold is crossed, not per frame.
- `motion.div` -> plain `div` on the root. NavBody/NavItems/menus keep framer.

### Verified
- Main-thread cost per scroll step: **/home 2.03 -> 0.58 ms (-71%)**,
  **/about 1.29 -> 0.40 ms (-69%)**.
- Behaviour identical on both routes: scroll down past 120 -> inline translate
  `0px -120px`; scroll up -> `0px`; computed `transition-property: translate`,
  `duration 0.3s`.
- Mobile shell states intact @390: floating class + `blur(12px)` when scrolled,
  cleared at top; logo and toggle present.
- Desktop @1266 intact: NavBody padding 32px at top -> 12px scrolled,
  `backdrop-blur-2xl` class appears on scroll and clears at top, root translate
  `0px -120px` / `0px`.
- NavBody still a motion.div in the page copy (8 `motion.div` remain); zero live
  `useScroll`/`useMotionValueEvent` references (the one grep hit is a comment).
- tsc clean, build compiled, biome **19 before and 19 after** (verified by
  stashing both files and re-linting).

### Still not addressed (flagged, not done)
The two navbar files are near-duplicates. Deduplicating them is the real
cleanup but it is a cross-route refactor, not this task's scope.

Scroll events are never delivered here (`scrollY 900`, `fired: 0`) and rAF is
frozen, so `visible` could not be driven by scrolling — the scrolled states were

## 2026-08-07 — AboutSection (homepage) mobile: stack -> smoke dissolve

**Task as written** named AboutTraditional on /about. That component has exactly
one card (the video) and nothing stacked — `ShrinkOnOverlap` and the sticky
wrappers are all `min-width: 768px`, so mobile /about is plain flow. Asked; the
user meant **AboutSection on the homepage**, i.e. `AboutImageStack`.

### What changed
`components/home/AboutImageStack.tsx` only. It is already the mobile-only
branch (`AboutSection` renders it under `!isDesktop`; desktop keeps its
framer/AnimatePresence stack), so desktop cannot be reached from this file.

- `SLOTS` (three peeking poses: y -16/-30, scale 0.94/0.88, opacity 0.85/0.7)
  replaced by `FRONT` / `HIDDEN`. Queued cards now sit at the identical pose
  with opacity 0 — nothing peeks above or behind the front card.
- `EXIT` changed from a drop (`y 56, scale 0.92`) to a dissipate:
  `y -22, scale 1.06, blur 12px, opacity 0`. Rises, expands, blurs out.
- `origin-top` -> `origin-center` so the expansion reads as spreading, not
  growing downward. Parent (`perspective-[1200px]`) has `overflow: visible`, so
  the 6% expansion is not clipped.
- Transition list: `transform, opacity, filter` for the front and leaving cards;
  **`opacity` alone** for queued cards. Two reasons — a released leaver drops
  its blur/scale instantly rather than spending 700ms animating a blur nobody
  can see, and opacity is never absent from the list, so a card promoted to
  front always has a transition already in place when its opacity flips.
  (First pass used `transition: none` for queued cards; that makes the fade-in
  depend on a transition appearing in the same commit as the value change.)

### Verified (prod build, `next start -p 3100`, 390x844)
Sampled React's **inline** styles (set synchronously, so unaffected by the
frozen transitions) across a full rotation — 8 distinct states, each of the
three cards taking its turn:
- exactly one card at `op:1` in every state — never two visible at once;
- every queued card `translate3d(0,0,0) scale(1) op:0 f:none` — no peek;
- every leaver `translate3d(0,-22px,0) scale(1.06) blur(12px) op:0 z:4`;
- after release the leaver returns to `scale(1) op:0 f:none z:1 tr:op-only` —
  snapped, no invisible blur animation;
- queued cards always `tr:op-only`.
- @1265 the host's first child is the framer card
  (`origin-bottom-right ... will-change-transform`, host 560px) — the mobile
  component is not mounted, desktop untouched.
- tsc clean; build compiled; biome clean on this file.

The preview pane reported `document.hidden: true`, which freezes CSS
transitions at their start values (every card read `opacity: 0`, `blur(0px)`

  Net effect: the section no longer has any rAF-driven background at all.

### `.jfif` needs next/image, not a bare <img>
Next's static handler has no mapping for the extension:
`GET /assets/carousel.jfif` -> `200 application/octet-stream` (44,699 B).
The optimizer sniffs content instead:
`GET /_next/image?url=%2Fassets%2Fcarousel.jfif&w=640&q=75` -> `200 image/jpeg`
(22,662 B). So routing through `<Image>` is what makes it serve as an image.

### Verified (prod build, `next start -p 3100`)
- @390: backdrop `display: block`, `maskImage: none`, no `.grid` in the panel,
  img box `390x591` with `object-fit: cover`, scrim `#0a0a0a / 0.65`.
  Forced the lazy load (browser lazy-loading is IO-driven and frozen in the
  pane): `img.decode()` resolved, `complete: true`,
  currentSrc `.../w=828&q=75`.
- @1265 desktop: backdrop `display: none`, panel 1266x800, section bg
  `rgb(10,10,10)`, 6 panels, h2 144px — unchanged.
- tsc clean; build compiled; biome back to the 2 pre-existing diagnostics
  (`noStaticElementInteractions` L442, `noArrayIndexKey` L572). The
  `noUnusedImports` this change introduced was fixed, not left.

### Flag: the source image is small
`carousel.jfif` is **347x195**. The mobile slide is 390x591 and uses
`object-cover`, so it upscales ~3x vertically — and more again at 2-3x DPR. It
will look soft. The 65% scrim hides some of it, but a ~1200x1800 source would
be the real fix. Delivered as asked; worth replacing the asset.

it clips vertically whether or not that was intended. Measured before the fix:

on the scroller's (`sr.bottom - cr.bottom === 0`), while `shadow-sm` reaches 4px
below the border box (`0 1px 3px 0` + `0 1px 2px -1px`). So ~4px was sheared off.

only for the top.

`max-md:pb-4 max-md:-mb-4` on the scroller. The padding gives the shadow room
INSIDE the scroll box; the equal negative margin takes that height back out of
the flow so nothing below moves.

**Report:** every clickable element on /home needs a double click; especially
Safari. User then narrowed it: **both** Mac and iOS Safari, and **always**, even
when the page has been stationary.

**No code was changed.** I could not identify a cause I can stand behind, and a
speculative page-wide change to this page is not worth the risk.

### Ruled out (each checked, not assumed)
- **Global overlay / z-index trap.** Hit-tested all 118 `a[href]`/`button` on the
  page, each scrolled to centre: 113 clean. See the 5 below.
- **The 5 "blocked" hits were a harness artifact, not a bug.** Portfolio's
  panel `<Link>` (`absolute inset-0 z-20`) read as covered by
  `p.whitespace-pre-line` = "Brands Directed" from `#stats`. Cause: the z-20
  wrapper carries `md:-mt-[100vh]`, and StatsSection's top measured 2028 —
  identical to `#portfolio`'s — because **no pins were active** (`.pin-spacer`
  count 0, fixed-pin count 0, ScrollTrigger never initialised). The preview pane
  delivers no scroll events and freezes rAF, so GSAP never runs and the negative
  margin is uncompensated. On the real site the pins absorb that overlap.
- **`pointer-events` toggling** — only static `pointer-events-auto` in
  per-service CtaSections, none on /home.
- **Page-wide `preventDefault`** — the only click suppressor on /home is
  BlogSection's drag guard (`onClickCapture`, `isPanning`), scoped to that track.

- **Page shell** — `layout.tsx` renders only `VideoViewportPause`, which returns
  `null`. No body-level overlay.
- **Lenis (`SmoothScroll`)** — skipped below 768px, so it cannot explain iOS.
- **Hover-latch (`group-hover:` on buttons)** — touch-only, cannot explain macOS.

The last two were my leading hypotheses; the user's "both browsers, always"
answer eliminates both.

### Why it could not be reproduced here
No Safari in this environment. The preview pane is Chromium AND is degraded:
no scroll events, frozen rAF, IntersectionObserver callbacks undelivered,
`document.hidden: true`. So GSAP pins, Lenis, scroll-linked state and CSS
transitions all fail to run — the exact machinery any remaining hypothesis
depends on.

### Next step — need a repro
Ask for: one specific element that misbehaves, and ideally a screen recording.
Most valuable single datapoint: whether the FIRST click fires any event at all
(paste in Safari's console, then click once):
`['pointerdown','pointerup','click'].forEach(t=>document.addEventListener(t,e=>console.log(t,e.target),true))`
If pointerdown/pointerup fire but `click` does not, the down and up targets
differ (something moves or is re-rendered under the pointer). If `click` fires
with the right target but nothing happens, it is a handler/navigation problem
instead. Those two point at opposite fixes.

## 2026-08-07 — Safari "needs two clicks" — diagnosed, fix applied (UNVERIFIED on Safari)

Follow-up to the previous entry. The user's Safari console gave the decisive
datapoint.

### The evidence
User aimed at a button; the logged event target was
`<p class="text-xl leading-[1.25em] text-zinc-600 font-regular max-md:text-lg">`
= AboutSection.tsx:166, with `same: true` (down and up agreed) and
`click` DID fire. So nothing is swallowing the click — **the click is landing on
the wrong element**. The "Connect With Us" `<Link>` (AboutSection.tsx:178) sits
immediately below that `<p>` in the same `space-y-6` stack.

Measured the geometry at 1280 wide, applying the exact end-state the
ScrollTrigger scrubs to (`translateY(40px) scale(0.85)`, `origin-top`) on
`aboutInnerRef`:
- link height **64px**
- layout centre `(144, 360)`, visual centre `(217, 313)`
- **vertical offset 46px** — more than half the link's height, so the visible
  button falls outside its own layout box
- element at the visual point in untransformed coords:
  `DIV.mt-10 max-w-2xl space-y-6` — the paragraph+button stack, and 46px up is
  the paragraph

i.e. WebKit hit-tests the composited layer against stale/untransformed geometry:
you click the button you can see, the event goes to the `<p>` behind it. Chrome
follows the transform, which is why it is Safari-only.

### What changed
`src/app/home/page.tsx` — dropped `md:will-change-transform` from the two GSAP
scrubbed wrappers (`aboutInnerRef`, `testimonialsInnerRef`). `will-change` is
what pins them into a permanently composited layer; without it WebKit
recomputes hit geometry from the live transform. GSAP still promotes the layer
for the duration of the tween, and the class was `md:`-gated so **mobile is
byte-identical**.

### Verified
- `willChange: "auto"` on both wrappers now; `origin-top` preserved.
- With the transform applied, the hit at the link's visual centre resolves to
  `SPAN` inside the Link (`hitIsInsideTheLink: true`) — no regression to the
  already-correct Chromium behaviour.
- tsc clean; build compiled; biome clean on the file.

### NOT verified — no Safari in this environment
This is a hypothesis-driven fix. The mechanism is well corroborated (user's log
+ the 46px measurement agree), but whether removing `will-change` is enough to
make WebKit recompute is untested. Confirmation snippet for Safari:

```
document.addEventListener('click', e => { const el = [...document.querySelectorAll('a,button')].find(n => { const r = n.getBoundingClientRect(); return e.clientX>=r.left&&e.clientX<=r.right&&e.clientY>=r.top&&e.clientY<=r.bottom; }); console.log('target:', e.target.tagName, '| geometry says:', el ? el.textContent.trim().slice(0,30) : 'none'); }, true)
```
If `target` is still a `P` while `geometry says` names the button, the layer is
still stale and the next step is to drop the scrubbed `scale` on the About /
Testimonials wrappers (the visual/layout mismatch itself), not just the hint.
